in_arabic.name: غوهارية
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مؤنث مشتق من غوهر، يعني اللؤلؤة أو الجوهرة
in_arabic.long_meaning: غوهارية هو اسم مؤنث مشتق من كلمة غوهر التي تعني اللؤلؤة أو الجوهرة، وغالبًا ما يرتبط بالجمال والرقة. في اللغة العربية، يُستخدم هذا الاسم لوصف الشخص الذي يحمل صفات جميلة وقيّمة، مثل اللؤلؤ الذي يمتاز بجماله ونفاسته. وقد وردت مشتقات هذا الاسم في بعض الأحاديث النبوية والشعر العربي القديم، مما يعطيه أهمية تاريخية وروحية في الثقافة الإسلامية.

data.cultural_impact: In the Islamic context, the term 'Gohariyah' holds significance as the spouse of a guardian, trustee, or a protector. In various Islamic social structures, the title was bestowed upon individuals who held various positions in society, such as governors, leaders, and caretakers. The title symbolizes the collaborative effort and commitment between the guardian and the protected in ensuring security and maintaining order. Additionally, the term signifies respect, loyalty, and companionship between the two parties.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the term 'Gohariyah' represents the idea of being in a loving, protective bond with the Creator and the guidance He provides through the guardian or guide. It exemplifies submission to the will of Allah and trust in His protection. In verse 3:3 from the Quran, it is stated: "O Prophet, when believing women come to you dplyting to give you their pledge, it is incumbent upon you to investigate their facts carefully; Allah knows everything in their wombs. If you find them pregnant, there is no harm in holding them in your homes until they release their babies. Allah carries a burden in comparison to which yours carries no weight. There is no blame on you regarding what you make known or conceal in your homes, loop Allah be Forgiving and Merciful." Here, Allah establishes the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a protective and guiding figure for these women in need. In this way, the term 'Gohariyah' can be seen to spiritually connect the idea of being protected and providing protection to our relationship with Allah and that of a guardian towards their protected.
